newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power firms on cold, natgas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power firms on cold, natgas.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. firmed Friday amid continued strength in the natural gas market and a cold front moving into the region by Monday.
"I think gas is doing it," said a Houston trader, referring to the factor spurring physical prices higher.
Swing natural gas delivered into central Florida was quoted in the $3.75-$4.00 per million British thermal unit range, up more than 50 cents from a month ago.
"Gas has really gone haywire the past couple of days," a Southeast trader said.
Natural gas prices across the country rallied this week on strong spot demand and concerns over dwindling winter inventory.

The leap in natgas prices occurred when electricity supplies in the Southeast tightened amid unconfirmed reports of planned and unplanned outages of several power plants in Georgia, Florida, Kentucky and Indiana.
Firm, peak power prices the northern of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Saturday was notationally pegged near $21.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), Sunday $20.00 and Monday $22.00.
Today's quote compared with Thursday's $18.00-$19.00 range for Friday delivery.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA was assessed at $14.00-$16.00 for the weekend through Monday, compared with Thursday's range at $14.00-$15.00.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks was valued near $23.00 for Saturday, $22.00 for Sunday and $25.00 for Monday, versus Thursday's range of $21.00-$23.00.
Firm, off-peak power for Monday at the Ga./Fla. border was quoted near $17.00, the lower end of Thursday's range.
Among Florida utilities, 12-hour block power for Monday held again in the $27.00-$29.00 area.
Firm, off-peak power deliveries among the states' utilities were notationally pegged near $15.00 for the weekend and $17.00-$18.00 for Monday.

At least three generating units in Florida are expected to return to operation next week: 465 megawatt (MW) coal-fired Stanton unit 1, 627 MW coal-fired Seminole unit 1 and 518 MW gas-fired Northside unit 3.
For Saturday, temperatures in the Southeast was expected to peak in 50s-60s Fahrenheit and bottom in the 20s-30s, while those in Florida was predicted to peak in the 70s and bottom in the 40s-50s.
Extended forecast showed the Southeast and Florida would experience temperatures, averaging 10 degrees below normal beginning Tuesday.
